scope: Original history-mode artwork. Character images are artistic interpretations, not documentary likenesses. No commercial original-game art is included.

assets.prompt_specification: Original ultra-wide Ming imperial study at dawn; folded memorials, brush, inkstone and bronze lamp on right; palace roofs and northern mountains beyond carved windows; ink wash, mineral pigments, parchment, charcoal, ochre and cinnabar; quiet left half for UI. No readable text, people, logos or modern/fantasy elements.

Original ultra-wide early Southern Song temporary court study; river reeds, supply boats, tiled roofs, rain and blue-green mountains; desk, memorials, celadon cup, brush and lamp on right; painted silk/mineral pigments in jade, slate and cream; quiet left half. No readable text, people, logos or copied commercial art.

Original 42-cell portrait atlas, exact 7 columns by 6 rows, no margins or gutters. Adult Ming eunuchs, ministers, scholars, commanders, a European Jesuit astronomer and rebel leaders. Distinct faces, both eyes open, full hats and shoulders, consistent scale and dark backgrounds; muted historically inspired painted robes and armor. No text, labels, modern or fantasy elements. Row-by-row role layout follows the original 42-person reference roster; final binding corrects the last-row portrait positions.

Original 40-cell portrait atlas, exact 8 columns by 5 rows, no margins or gutters. Southern Song emperor, court officials, scholars, naval and army commanders, distinct adult faces with open eyes; Song futou hats, muted robes and practical armor, same framing and dark backgrounds. No labels, numbering, modern or fantasy elements. Roster order follows the 40-person scenario data.

Original 80-cell portrait atlas, exact 10 columns by 8 rows, equal square cells, no margins/gutters/text. First 22 military officers, next 16 civil officials, six rebels, five engineer-scholars, eight young adult future talents, and remaining court officials/censors/governors. Distinct adult faces, open eyes, full hats and shoulders, historically inspired Ming robes and armor, consistent dark neutral backgrounds.
